stories.headline: DUTCH TO INTERN FORMER KAISER; Holland Embarrassed by His Presence--Officials Go to Confer with Him. REMAINS ON RAILWAY TRAIN Three More German Rulers Ousted--All the Rest Likely to Go. Said to Have Planned Internment. DUTCH TO INTERN FORMER KAISER

stories.headline: MOONEY SENTENCE IS COMMUTED TO PRISON FOR LIFE; California Governor Saves from Gallows Labor Leader Convicted of Bomb Murder. Motives of Anarchism. President Wilson's Messages. MOONEY SENTENCE IS COMMUTED Labor Demands a New Trial. Will Carry Out Protest Strike. New York Leaders Not Satisfied. FIGHT TO SAVE MOONEY. Labor Made His Case Its Own, Both Here and Abroad. RED FLAG IN SAN FRANCISCO Several Members of the Bolshevist Group Rounded Up by Police.

stories.headline: U.S. AND NEW YORK AGREE ON DISPOSING OF NUCLEAR WASTES
stories.summary: Energy Adm accepts responsibility for eventual disposal outside NYS of huge deposits of highly radioactive nuclear waste at West Valley, NY, storage facility; Carey adm agrees in turn to accept additional amounts of nuclear waste produced by nuclear reactors around NYS for interim storage at West Valley until Fed Govt comes up with plan for eventual disposal; agreement was reached by Sec Schlesinger and James L Larocca, State Energy Comr; Sen Daniel Moynihan says he had assurances from Schlesinger on Fed takeover a yr and a half ago; Fed Budget Office must still approve plan, which could cost Fed Govt estimated $200 million to $1.1 billion and take 10 yrs; kinds of wastes stored at facility, which is owned by state and leased to Nuclear Fuel Services, noted; map; illus (M)

stories.headline: ‘Free‐for‐All’ Or Stability?; Analysts of Oil Industry Differ on World Outlook Seasonal Slump Cited Free‐for‐All’ or Stability? Analysts’ Outlooks Differ Question of ‘Production Rationing’ Need to Rebuild Inventories
stories.summary: analysis of OPEC's decision; says oil economists are not as concerned about rise in base price as they are about sanctioning of individual members' premiums; notes hope that supply situation may ease, taking upward pressure off prices; says big unknown is whether OPEC will be able to restrain production, thus keeping things tight as Iranian oil continues to re‐enter mkt; comments by Theodore R Eck (Indiana Standard), Exxon, Walter J Levy and John H Lichtblau (Petroleum Indus Research Foundation) (M)

stories.headline: CARTER, NEARING END OF VISIT, TO SEE BEGINAND SADAT AGAIN; OBSTACLES STILL BLOCK A PACT
stories.summary: Pres Carter has been unable to reconcile difficult issues holding up conclusion of peace treaty; scores Begin and Sadat for refusing to 'take a chance' for peace; will meet separately with them before returning to US in effort to complete treaty; illus (M)

stories.headline: CANADA FINDS RISE OF 28% IN GAS SALES TO U.S. IS FEASIBLE
stories.summary: Canada's Natl Energy Bd approves 28% increase in gas exports to US, citing more optimistic estimates of Canadian reserves and more pessimistic estimate of Canadian econ activity (M)
